title: load_attachments_for_messages uses dynamic SQL with varying IN clause, bypassing prepare_cached
description: load_attachments_for_messages() builds a SQL string with N '?' placeholders matching the message count, then calls conn.prepare() (not prepare_cached()). The code comment acknowledges this but calls it necessary to avoid unbounded cache growth. In practice, list_by_chat() fetches up to 'limit' messages per call, so the placeholder count is bounded by the limit parameter (typically 50-100). An alternative avoiding dynamic SQL entirely: batch the attachment lookup with a JOIN against a temporary table or use repeated single-message queries. For the Phase 1 single-user case with small limits this is not a hot path, but the prepare() call creates and destroys a prepared statement on every list_by_chat() invocation. A capped LRU prepare cache (e.g., sizes 1, 10, 25, 50, 100) would eliminate the allocation on common page sizes.
